### Impact

An unauthenticated attacker can bypass server-side controls that match on the request path of a page route.

title: sqlite3-ruby: Possible SQL query truncation when a string is 4 GiB or larger
description:
### Summary

sqlite3-ruby cast Ruby string lengths (`long`) to `int` before passing them to SQLite. On 64-bit platforms, a string of 4 GiB (2^32 bytes) or larger had its length wrap, so SQLite saw only the first `length mod 2^32` bytes. An attacker who controls the length of a SQL string could truncate the query, for example dropping a trailing `WHERE` clause. The affected paths are:

title: rails-html-sanitizer: Possible XSS via shared scrubber state in concurrent calls
description:
## Summary

Two concurrent `sanitize` calls with different `tags:` or `attributes:` options can interleave, so one call is scrubbed with the other call's allowlist.

- Fixed versions: `1.7.2`

title: Addressable: Regular Expression Denial of Service in templates with certain exploded expressions
description:
### Impact

Within the URI template implementation in Addressable, templates using the `*` (explode) modifier with the `/`, `.`, `;`, `?` or `&` operators (e.g., `{/segments*}`, `{.ext*}`, `{;params*}`, `{?query*}`) generate regular expressions vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking. When `Template#match` or `Template#extract` is called with a maliciously crafted URI that starts with the operator's leading character, matching takes exponential time, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption and denial of service. An input under 60 bytes is enough to occupy a thread for minutes.

title: vm2: timeout Option Bypass via FinalizationRegistry Cleanup Callback (Unbounded Host Event-Loop Block)
description:
### Vulnerability Summary
 
vm2's `VM({ timeout })` option is documented and relied upon as the mechanism that bounds how long sandboxed code may execute. It does not, and structurally cannot, bound code that the V8 engine itself schedules to run *after* that call has already returned.

### Impact
For SCRAM, and for Digest with mutual authentication, the client computes the server's verification value (the SCRAM ServerSignature, or the Digest rspauth) but does not act on the result. If the value is present and does not verify, the client only logs it and still delivers the response to the application as a successful, authenticated result. A server that never proved knowledge of the shared secret is accepted, so the client loses its ability to detect an impostor. ## Unbounded Remote Media Fetch and Video Frame Expansion DoS

### Summary
The `POST /v1/chat/completions` endpoint in mistral.rs fetches attacker-supplied media URLs (image, audio, video) into server memory with no byte limit, and extracts every frame of a supplied video when `num_frames` is `None`. Any authenticated user who knows a folder's id can put a chat of their own into another user's folder, including a shared folder where they hold read-only access and a folder they have no access to at all. The chat then shows up in that folder for everyone who can read it, under a title and with content the attacker controls. | 16 KB | 224 ms |
| 64 KB | 4.4 s |
| 128 KB | 18.5 s |

title: postgres-protocol: Unbounded SCRAM iteration count allows a malicious server to cause CPU-exhaustion denial of service
description:
A malicious, compromised, or man-in-the-middle server can supply an arbitrarily
large SCRAM-SHA-256 PBKDF2 iteration count during authentication. The client

title: MCP PHP SDK: client HttpTransport SSE buffer (sseBuffer .= chunk) grows unbounded when server withholds the event delimiter
description:
## Summary

The HTTP client transport in `mcp/sdk` reads a Server-Sent-Events (SSE) response
stream incrementally and appends each 4 KiB chunk to an in-memory buffer
(`$this->sseBuffer .= $chunk;`) with **no upper bound**. The buffer is only ever
flushed when an SSE event delimiter (`"\n\n"`) appears. A remote MCP server (the
peer the client connects to) that streams response bytes without ever sending the
`"\n\n"` delimiter makes `$sseBuffer` grow without limit until the client process
exhausts its PHP `memory_limit` (fatal "Allowed memory size … exhausted") or is
killed by the OS OOM-killer.
